theoretical_curve_batch_one.model: step_ms = W/BW + KV_read_floor + compute_residual; W=18.52 GB, pure-read BW=182.5 GB/s
theoretical_curve_batch_one.p40000_absolute_ceiling: CORRECTED 2026-09-26 (supersedes the L2-absorption paragraph of the same date): the 6x GQA-redundant V read in the values kernel is a REAL DRAM cost, not L2-absorbed. The values kernel's 40.3 ms/layer at S=40000 is within noise of the pure-DRAM time for its 6x requested volume (7.86 GB / 182.5 GB/s = 43 ms); the '195 GB/s' figure is requested volume divided by wall time and only marginally exceeds the 182.5 GB/s pure-read ceiling (noise range), not a proof of L2 absorption. The split-chunk GQA-shared values kernel (1x V read) measures 1.68x faster per layer in the microbenchmark and 1.17x faster per decode step on the real P40000 API (193.0 -> 165.2 ms/step), proving the redundancy is a real bandwidth cost. The realistic batch-one ceiling with the split values path is weight floor 101.5 + split values ~24.0 + scores 38.6 + launch ~0.7 = ~165 ms/step (~6.1 tok/s); the measured split-path 165.2 ms/step (6.05 tok/s) matches it. The 10 tok/s target (100 ms/step) remains below the 101.5 ms weight-read floor and is unreachable for batch-one on this device.

target_reachability.claim: 10 tok/s (100 ms/step) is below the batch-one weight-read hardware floor of 101.5 ms (9.85 tok/s) for this model on this device
target_reachability.evidence: same-workload hardware bound: W=18.52 GB exact per-step read / 182.5 GB/s measured pure-read ceiling; matched profile: GEMV path runs at ~100% of the measured pure-read ceiling (floor 101.5 ms vs measured 103.17 ms intercept from 3-point fit); reconciliation: no known implementation can read 18.52 GB per step in <100 ms on this device
target_reachability.attention_kv_read_efficiency: CORRECTED 2026-09-26 (supersedes the L2-absorption paragraph of the same date): the '195 GB/s values / 204 GB/s scores, both above the DRAM ceiling, therefore L2-absorbed' reasoning is invalid. 195 GB/s is only ~7% above the 182.5 GB/s measured pure-read ceiling -- inside the measurement noise band -- and the values kernel's 40.3 ms/layer matches the 43 ms pure-DRAM time for its 6x-redundant 7.86 GB/layer requested volume. The split-chunk GQA-shared values kernel, which reads each V row once (1.31 GB/layer), runs 1.68x faster per layer in the microbenchmark (1.689 vs 2.799 ms) and cuts the real P40000 decode step by 27.8 ms (193.0 -> 165.2 ms/step). The 6x GQA redundancy is therefore a real DRAM bandwidth cost, and the GEMV weight path (179.5 GB/s, 98.4% of the ceiling) remains the dominant DRAM-bound component.

owner_decision_request: 10 tok/s target exceeds the batch-one hardware floor. Options requiring owner ruling: (a) change contract to batched decode (multiple concurrent requests amortize the 18.52 GB weight read); (b) lower weight quantization (accuracy risk, out of current production accuracy scope); (c) re-set the P40000 target to a reachable value (e.g. 8 tok/s absolute ceiling is ~8.6, realistic ~5.2 after unroll-128). This record does not select a route or change the target.

l2_absorption_and_smem_merge.finding: CORRECTED 2026-09-26 (supersedes the L2-absorption finding of the same date): the 6x GQA redundant K/V reads are NOT absorbed by L2 at near-zero DRAM cost. The values kernel's 40.3 ms/layer at S=40000 equals, within noise, the pure-DRAM time for its 6x requested volume (7.86 GB / 182.5 GB/s = 43 ms), and the split-chunk GQA-shared kernel (1x V read, 1.31 GB/layer) is 1.68x faster per layer in the microbenchmark and 1.17x faster per decode step on the real P40000 API. The GEMV weight path runs at 179.5 GB/s (98.4% of the DRAM ceiling) and is the true DRAM-bound component; the values kernel's 6x redundancy is a second, smaller, real DRAM cost.

smem_gqa_merge.name: shared-memory GQA merge: one block per KV head serves all 6 query heads from a single smem V tile, reducing the V read from 6x to 1x
smem_gqa_merge.bit_exact: PASS (S=1024 vs CPU oracle, 0/6144 diff) -- the per-(query,dimension) position-ordered FMA sequence is preserved, so the BF16 output is bit-identical
smem_gqa_merge.occupancy: prod 24 blocks x 256 thr (6 blocks/SM); smem 4 blocks x 1024 thr (1 block/SM, sm_87 max 1024 thr/block)
smem_gqa_merge.verdict: re-measured 2026-09-26: the 1024-thread single-block-per-KV-head variant is indeed 3.19x slower (occupancy collapse to 1 block/SM), but the original rejection reason ('the 6x redundancy was already free via L2') is WRONG. A 512-thread split-chunk variant (grid (chunks, 4), 32 KiB dynamic smem per block, 6 query heads per 256-thread group, atomicAdd combine) reads each V row once and measures 1.68x FASTER than the production kernel in the microbenchmark (1.689 vs 2.799 ms/layer at S=40000) and 1.17x faster per decode step on the real P40000 API (165.2 vs 193.0 ms/step). The 6x redundancy is a real DRAM cost; the smem merge is the correct fix, at the cost of bit-exactness (see qwen36-27b-decode-split-values-e2e-2026-09-26.json).
